surfaces.part: ramp slope with chevron tread pattern, climbing north
flat ground apron in front of the ramp

answer.evidence: The width is a constant 32 px for all 80 rows. Rows 0-63 show the ramp as a sloped surface seen from above, with chevron tread marks pointing north. A dark outline along the left edge and a dark line at row 63 separate it from the ground. The cliff-wall strips at the left (about x 0-9) and right (about x 29-31) are drawn as flat textured bands, with no receding side face. Rows 64-79 are plain flat ground. No vertical south face of 3 or more rows is drawn, so this reads as a flat top-down slab. The apron is floor, not a front face, and the ramp has no riser.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate has 7 visible tones per tile, equal to the paving reference and above the grass reference's 3. Near-flat coverage is 16%, low but not zero, and probably sits in the sandy bottom strip and parts of the ramp centre. Only 18% of its dark edge pixels are neutral, so the edges lean brown and grey-brown against the cliff and ramp material, which reads as a dark material tone and not a sticker line. The chevron tread pattern on the ramp has light and dark steps, and the cliff walls on both sides carry grain, so the ramp has real structure. It has about 5 ramp steps against the references' 5-6, which is slightly below but acceptable. The sand foot is the flattest area, with only light speckle, but it is not a large dead fill. Overall it would sit acceptably next to the references.

answer.evidence: Rows 0-63 show a large sloped ramp plane with repeating chevron tread rows (light chevron lines in x=16 at rows 1, 3, 7, 13, 20, and so on). A dark outline along the left edge (rows 5-63) and a dark bottom edge at row 63 separate it from the cliff-cut walls. The left wall is a darker vertical face about 8-10 px wide, rows 5-63, and a thinner darker wall strip runs on the right. Rows 64-79 are flat light floor at the foot of the ramp. The ramp is a foreshortened inclined top surface, not a flat top-down slab. The vertical faces counted as front_face_rows are the side cut walls; there is no separate south face. This reading is borderline for a ramp tile.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate matches the paving reference on visible tones per tile (7 vs 7) and is above the grass reference (3). Its dark edge pixels are only 18% neutral, so the side edges are a tinted brown-grey rather than a black sticker line. The structure is readable: chevron scallop ridges on the ramp face, darker side walls, and a sandy landing at the bottom. Against that, near-flat coverage is 16% while both references are at 0%. The sandy band at the bottom and the wide ramp-face areas between chevron lines are visibly flat, with little speckle or grain. Each chevron is a single-tone line with no per-ridge highlight, unlike Beodeul's stone-by-stone shading. The candidate has about 5 steps, against about 6 in the references, and only 11 distinct colours in total. It is clean and tinted, but a careful artist would likely find it slightly flatter and thinner than the references, so it fails.
